name: Japan Rose
lede: Japan Rose is a moderate, yellowish pink built from the word rose, over-represented in Indian paintings despite its name.

sections.title: A rose, not a place
sections.body:
The library records Japan Rose from Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary, plate 3 A 10, first recorded 1912 [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[pinkish-tan]], [[fawn]], [[fawn]] and [[light-russet-vinaceous]], at 2.8, 3.5, 
In LCH terms it measures lightness 69, chroma 24, hue 49 degrees, the ISCC-NBS "moderate yellowish pink" block, Munsell 1.7YR 6.8/4.5, between [[pink]] and [[orange]] [1]. 8, 3.5, 3.5 and 3.6 ΔE [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive finds this color in 419 of 23,781 paintings, 1.76 percent, as photographed; the within-painting lens finds it in 210 [2]. That makes it more common than 72 percent of the named colors we track [2]. It peaks in the 1900s, in 25 of 1,674 paintings, at 1.5 percent of that century's paintings, 1.6 times the expected rate, and it is over-represented in Indian paintings, 2.5 times expected, 41 of 721 [2]. Inside a painting it most often sits as a light, in 40 percent of its appearances [2].

Christen Købke is its most devoted painter, carrying it in 5 of his 50 works here, 5.9 times the baseline [2]. The earliest match is dated 1230, by Berlinghiero; that is 700 years before the name's own first record, in 1930, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2].
